body:
AI Data Giant Raises at Record Valuation

Databricks announced on Thursday a new funding round valuing the company at $188 billion, led by Coatue Management. The round, reportedly worth approximately $3 billion according to the Wall Street Journal, cements Databricks' position as one of the most valuable private companies in the world.

The company has been on a remarkable fundraising trajectory. Just five months ago, in February, Databricks closed a $5 billion Series L at a $134 billion valuation. Five months before that, it raised $1 billion at $100 billion. And in December 2024, it raised a then-record $10 billion at $62 billion — meaning the company has roughly tripled its valuation in 18 months.

From Big Data to AI Powerhouse

Founded in 2013, Databricks initially built its reputation in the big data era with software enabling enterprises to store massive amounts of data in the cloud while producing fast analytics. Because it already sat on troves of enterprise data, the company was well-positioned when businesses began demanding AI with the same security and governance they expect from traditional software.

The company has rolled out a series of AI products including Lakebase, a database built for AI agents, and Unity, its AI gateway, along with Omnigent, a "meta-harness" that manages multiple AI agents. CEO Ali Ghodsi has positioned the company as a champion of affordable, open-weight AI models.

Open Models and Cost Control

Databricks has become one of the biggest advocates for using open-weight AI models — particularly Z.ai's GLM 5.2 — for cost control, one of the defining enterprise AI trends of 2026. Last week, Ghodsi shared internal benchmarking results from managing AI costs across the company's 3,000 software engineers.

The benchmarks found that open models could handle even the most complex coding tasks at significantly lower cost than proprietary alternatives from Anthropic and OpenAI. Equally important, the choice of agentic coding harness impacted costs just as much as the model itself.

What It Means for Indian Tech Professionals

Databricks' rise has significant implications for the Indian tech ecosystem. The company employs a substantial number of Indian-origin engineers, and its platform is widely used across Indian IT services companies. As enterprises globally shift toward AI-native data infrastructure, Indian tech professionals with Databricks expertise are increasingly in demand.

The company's embrace of open-weight models aligns with India's own push toward AI sovereignty and cost-effective AI deployment, making its tools particularly relevant for Indian startups navigating the AI transition.

Sources: TechCrunch, Wall Street Journal
